findings.title: Constructor requireNonNull checks wrong variable for rawTokenId
findings.body: The fourth argument of the constructor is `String rawTokenId`, but the validation reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. The check uses `grantType` (already validated on the previous line) and so cannot fail. As a result `rawTokenId` is never validated and a null raw token id silently passes the constructor and is later encoded into the produced token id. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring range; does not actually verify the grant shortcut
findings.body:
The body asserts: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; return isUUID().matches(items[1]);`. Two defects combine to make the filter useless:
1) The negation is missing - the substring must equal the expected shortcut for the match to succeed, but the code rejects matches instead.
2) The indices are wrong - the grant-type shortcut occupies positions 4-5 of the prefix (session[0..1], token[2..3], grant[4..5]), so extracting `substring(3, 5)` returns the second character of the token-type shortcut and the first character of the grant shortcut (`ta` for `onrtac`), never the two-char grant shortcut the test expects.

Concretely, for `AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT = "ac"`, the encoded prefix `onrtac` produces substring `"ta"`, which never equals `"ac"`, so the test falls through to the UUID check and the matcher matches every well-formed id regardless of grant type. For refresh tokens the substring `(online/offline, regular, refresh)` becomes `"rt"`, which DOES equal the expected shortcut and incorrectly FAILS the match. Fix to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: Converting getShouldUseLightweightToken from instance method to public static is a behavioral break for subclasses
findings.body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken` was previously a package-private instance method. The change turns it into `public static boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...)`. Any custom subclass outside the tree (or within) that overrode this method to influence which token type is chosen will silently stop being called - static methods are not dispatched virtually, and their overrides no longer compile cleanly. The PR description does not call this out as an API/SPI change. If the method is meant to be part of an extension contract it should be made `public` only while staying an instance method (or factored into a separate strategy class).

findings.title: No null check on getShortcut() before using shortcut as map key and in token id encoding
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType` invokes `factory.getShortcut()` and uses the result as both a map key (`grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)`) and as part of the produced token id (`+ grantShort +` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`). The interface contract `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not forbid null. A custom or future factory returning null would either corrupt the `grantsByShortcuts` map (ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys, throwing NullPointerException) or cause `encodeTokenId` to concatenate a null piece into the encoded token id (also raising NPE). Add a null-check or document that implementations must return a non-null 2-character shortcut.

findings.title: Pair of map updates not atomic; transient inconsistency possible under concurrent refresh
findings.body: `getShortcutByGrantType` performs `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType); grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut);` as two separate operations. Concurrent callers loading a brand new grant type can leave the cache in a window where one direction (shortcut -> grant type) is populated and the other (grant type -> shortcut) is not yet visible. A concurrent reader doing the opposite lookup at that moment will not find the entry and may either retry (incurring an extra `getProviderFactoriesStream` enumeration) or - in the `encodeTokenId` path - throw IllegalStateException("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType") despite the grant being known moments later. Although very unlikely in practice, the two maps are mutated independently under contention; an `AtomicReference<Map<...>>` swap or populating both into temporary maps and then performing atomic `putAll` would be safer.

findings.title: grantType field is cached from form params at construction but not refreshed when setFormParams is called later
findings.body: The Context constructor takes the grant type from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and stores it in `this.grantType`. The class also exposes `setFormParams(...)` which replaces `this.formParams` but does not update `this.grantType`. If a grant flow modifies form parameters after construction, `context.getGrantType()` (now used by `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process` to populate `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`) will return the stale value, causing the encoded `grantType` shortcut in the access token id to be wrong. Update `setFormParams` to recompute `grantType` from the new params or document that the value is intentionally fixed at construction.

findings.title: SpI is marked internal but the PR description advertises extensibility for custom encodings
findings.body: `TokenContextEncoderSpi.isInternal()` returns `true`, meaning no custom `TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` implementations can be registered through the normal Spi lookup. The PR description states the SpI was introduced so that "someone (can) introduce his own provider ... and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc." These two statements are mutually exclusive: if the SpI is internal, downstream implementations cannot plug in. Either the SpI should be public (and `isInternal()` should return `false`), or the PR description should be corrected and the indirection justified purely for testability - in which case the `TokenContextEncoderProvider`/`...Factory` types could live in a single class without an SpI.
